cells.tense: Right now the weight between you is where it should be, and you carry your share without keeping score.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Point your effort one direction this week — your own pick, not the place it's needed most — and work there, letting the other things wait.
cells.core:
Strength moves between you and the ones you're beside, and the amounts come out right. What you put in returns, nobody carries more than their part, and that's what keeps it steady. Steady like this, it's free to feed direction: not strength spread thinner over more of them, but strength aimed at something on purpose.

So pick the heading before the week fills up. One direction for your own effort, chosen because you want it, not because somebody's short. Then stop scanning the room for what else needs you. You'll feel the pull to keep looking — things you've been holding will wave from the side. Let them wave. What you already carry stays yours; the new part is only the aim. Keep the load fair while you're at it, because fair is what makes aiming last.
cells.sheetLine: The weight is fair, and now your strength can be aimed.
cells.verb: spending your own strength so the ones beside you can stand
cells.place: where the load between two people gets weighed and corrected

cells.tense: In the weeks ahead you'll be watching the scales before anything has been asked of you, keeping shares even on paper nobody asked to see.
cells.act: let the inner compass decide the small case
cells.ask: At the next small debt — a few dollars, a favor, a reply owed — settle it once from gut sense and stop, closing the ledger there.
cells.core:
You give so the weights come out even, and you're already checking the next several rounds in advance. Every gap gets measured before it opens. From outside it looks generous; from inside it doesn't land, because a scale that keeps wanting to be checked can't rest, and neither can the ones standing on it.

There's a steadier place to run this from: the quiet sense of what's right that doesn't need arithmetic. Settle one small debt this week — money, a returned favor, a reply you owe — from that sense, once, and leave the record of it alone. You'll feel the pull to audit it by Thursday. Let the audit go. The evenness you've been buying with all that measuring is already in your hands.

cells.tense: The flow of strength between you and the ones beside you stopped moving awhile back, and you're still at the old arrangement.
cells.act: let the friction test what you are committed to
cells.ask: Set something you still hold for someone against real resistance this week — the awkward ask, the true number — and let what happens tell you what holds.
cells.core:
What passes between you and the others has gone quiet. The arrangement you had still stands in your head, but nothing moves through it now. You keep your own, and wait to find out whether re-entering is worth it. It isn't a choice you made — it's a doorway you've been standing at since it shut.

The way through isn't more giving, and it isn't feeling your way in. Take one commitment you still carry and set it against something that pushes back — the part you've been steering around because it might end. Maybe it ends. Maybe it holds. Either way the testing is the point, and whatever falls away was the method, not the commitment. Let something meet real resistance this week and see what holds.

cells.tense: The balancing keeps happening through your hands, and your own account of it names luck instead of you.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: When you catch yourself setting something right between two people, hold a second and know your hand is in it, then do it anyway — no announcement.
cells.core:
You re-balance things for the ones near you — absorb the shortfall, step back, say the sentence that settles it — and it doesn't register as anything done. It's just how the room goes. The hand on the scale is yours; your words for it are mood, timing, chemistry. The ones on the other end don't file it that way.

Nothing needs announcing, and nothing needs discussing. Steer the direction you already steer and stop checking whether it counts. When you're setting something even without a word, hold a beat and register that the correction is coming from you, then make it anyway. One second of knowing, and the skill stops being background. The weighing was yours the whole time. Only the name was missing.
cells.sheetLine: The hand evening things out is yours, filed under luck.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is quietly covering gaps for others and calling it circumstance; the record supports the seat (fair calibration) and the disowned present, but not any particular act of covering, so the cell says only that the even-ing-up happens with no name on it. A reader could say the giving is simply practical, or that nothing is one-sided at all; the ask (before the next quiet correction, pause long enough to know you are doing it) is still usable either way, since noticing the act does not depend on my read being right. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'talk about it, and you'll say the whole thing just evens out,' so the draft drops the quotation mark and leaves the person room to say no.
